'''Thomas Anthony Garrity''' (born 25 April 1959)<ref name=":1" /> is an American mathematician. He teaches at Williams College, where he is the Webster Atwell Class of 1921 Professor of Mathematics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Thomas Garrity |url=https://math.williams.edu/thomas-garrity/ |access-date=2023-02-20 |website=Mathematics & Statistics |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Thomas Anthony Garrity was born in 1959.<ref name=":1">Birth year from [https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2001002291.html Library of Congress catalog entry], retrieved 2024-04-05</ref> He completed his bachelor's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1981.<ref name=":0" /> He attended [[Brown University]] for doctoral studies, completing a PhD in mathematics in 1986 under the supervision of professor [[William Fulton (mathematician)|William Fulton]]. Garrity's doctoral thesis was titled ''On Ample [[Vector bundle|Vector Bundles]] and Negative Curvature''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garrity |first=Thomas |date=December 2021 |title=Curriculum Vitae of Thomas A. Garrity |url=https://math.williams.edu/files/2022/01/cvgarrityDecember-2021.pdf}}</ref>

== Career ==

Garrity is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Williams College]], where he has taught since 1989.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://math.williams.edu/thomas-garrity/ | title=Thomas Garrity }}</ref>

=== Research ===
In 1989, Garrity and three other collaborators found an algorithm in [[NC (complexity)|NC]] to factorize [[rational polynomials]] over the [[complex numbers]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bajaj |first1=Chanderjit |last2=Canny |first2=John |last3=Garrity |first3=Thomas |last4=Warren |first4=Joe |date=1989 |title=Factoring Rational Polynomials over the Complex Numbers |url=https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~bajaj/cvc/papers/1989/journal/p81-bajaj.pdf |journal=SIAM Journal on Computing |language=en |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=318–331 |doi=10.1137/0222024 |issn=0097-5397}}</ref>

In 1991, Garrity discovered the concept of "geometric continuity", which generalizes several other notions of continuity for both explicit and [[implicit surfaces]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Garrity |first1=Thomas |last2=Warren |first2=Joe |date=February 1991 |title=Geometric continuity |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/0167-8396(91)90049-H |journal=Computer Aided Geometric Design |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=51–65 |doi=10.1016/0167-8396(91)90049-h |issn=0167-8396|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1999, Garrity came up with the concept of a ''simplex sequence'', which is an alternate approach to the [[Hermite problem]] (of which the [[Jacobi-Perron algorithm]] is yet another approach).<ref name=":2">{{cite journal
 | last = Garrity | first = Thomas
 | arxiv = math/9906016
 | doi = 10.1006/jnth.2000.2608
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of Number Theory
 | mr = 1825992
 | pages = 86–103
 | title = On periodic sequences for algebraic numbers
 | volume = 88
 | year = 2001}}</ref> For the case of ordered pairs, if the simplex sequence is eventually periodic, then the two numbers must be of degree at most three.<ref name=":2" />

==Recognition==
Garrity was a 2004 recipient of one of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/200405/comm-maa.pdf|title=MAA Awards Presented in Phoenix|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|pages=544–545|date=May 2004|volume=51|issue=5}}</ref>
